statements.t: We believe that our emphasis on maximizing productivity alongside targeted marketing investments will support our ability to drive sustained, profitable growth in 2027 and 2028.”

These increases were the result of favorable segment, brand and channel mix as well as lower than expected destruction costs driven by our inventory efficiency programs, which were partially offset by higher tariff expenses.

As shared last quarter, we are reinvesting the tariff refunds to support the strong momentum we are seeing in the United States market, drive our top-line growth and position the Company for a successful 2027; as such, we anticipate our full year 2026 A&P expenditures will approach our long-term target of approximately 21% of net sales.
The Company is increasing its 2026 sales outlook from $1.48 billion to $1.49 billion and maintaining EPS of $4.85.
EPS guidance for 2026 includes the expected effect of refunds already received associated with approximately $17.7 million of estimated IEEPA tariffs paid by the Company.

As of September 30, 2026, the Company has recognized $16.4 million of these refunds in its Condensed Consolidated Statements of Income, with the majority of the remaining $1.4 million expected to be realized in the current fourth quarter.
The Company’s regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.80 per share will be paid on December 31, 2026 to shareholders of record on December 15, 2026.

dropped.t: Madar concluded, “While some aspects of the market environment remain challenging, we are encouraged by the trajectory of our business and maintain a measured but positive outlook for the balance of the year, 2027 and beyond.”
